cells: Removal of loose particles leading to lowering of land surface.
Sand-laden winds polish, groove, and cut rock surfaces.
Particles collide and become smaller and rounded.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Wind erosion in arid environments operates primarily through two distinct mechanisms: Deflation and Abrasion.
Deflation landforms are created by the lifting, blowing, and removal of loose, dry, fine dust and sand particles from the ground.
Abrasion landforms result from the mechanical sandblasting action of wind-borne grains striking exposed rock surfaces.
Deflation forms hollows, blowouts, and desert pavements, while Abrasion sculpters mushroom rocks, yardangs, and zeugens.

blocks.content: • Deflation Hollows – depressions created by intense removal of sediments.
• Desert Pavement (Reg) – surface of coarse pebbles after fine materials are removed.
• Lag Deposits – accumulation of heavier particles left behind after deflation.
• Playas – dry lake beds formed in desert basins.

rows: Lifting and removal of loose particles by wind
Sandblasting and grinding of rocks by wind-blown particles
Mechanical wear, tear, and sculpting of exposed rocks

blocks.content: • Dreikanter – three-faced ventifacts shaped by shifting winds.
• Yardangs – elongated ridges aligned with prevailing winds.

items: Competitive exams frequently ask candidates to classify specific landforms as either Deflation or Abrasion features.
Mushroom rocks (Gour), Yardangs, and Zeugens are classic examples of Abrasion landforms.
Blowouts and deflation hollows (often forming oasis basins) are direct results of Deflation.

blocks.content: • Zeugens – tabular ridges with resistant cap rock.
• Rock Pedestals (Mushroom Rocks) – undercut bases due to intense near-ground abrasion.
• Inselbergs – isolated resistant rock hills rising from desert plains.
